skills.skill: I can choose a survey sample.

items.q: If a representative sample of $20$ people is to be taken from a group of $280$ children and $120$ adults, how many adults should be chosen?
items.src: Oxford Maths 10 VC (2022), Ch 10 review, multiple-choice Q10 (p. 566)

items.q:
A survey is conducted to determine how many siblings children have. Which of the following methods of conducting the survey is more likely to lead to bias?
Method 1: Choosing $20$ children at random from a school.
Method 2: Asking $20$ children waiting outside a primary school at the end of a day.
sol: Method 2: children waiting outside a primary school at the end of the day are more likely to be picking up a younger brother or sister, so they are more likely to have siblings.
items.src: Cambridge Essential Mathematics 8 (3rd Ed), Exercise 8F Q4c (p. 585); adapted: stem from Q4 kept, graph and parts a–b left out
